newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain and France may send rapid force to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Spain and France may send rapid force to Zaire.

text.p: Spain and France could send a U.N.-approved rapid deployment force to aid refugees in Zaire ahead of a relief operation organised by the United Nations, a Defence Ministry spokesman said on Friday.

"The United Nations is going to send its own task force but before, with more urgency, the U.N. may allow the dispatch of a rapid force," the spokesman told Reuters. "It may only be Spain and France."
The multinational force approved by the U.N. could be assembled quickly, ahead of a task force actually organised by the U.N. which could take a month, the spokesman said.
Spain would not send any troops before the United Nations gave its approval, however, the spokesman said.
He said Spain was prepared immediately to send 300 soldiers in an initial deployment and was still considering whether it would send more in later stages of the operation.

Earlier, Spanish Defence Minister Eduardo Serra said troops were on alert to prepare for an immediate intervention, should that be possible. The force would open humanitarian corridors to facilitate aid to more than a million refugees in eastern Zaire.
